title: AI Continuous Assessment Loop: AI drives the entire assessment as an iterative observe-decide-execute cycle until maximum depth reached or stuck — replaces fixed phases
goal: Replace the fixed Phase 1/Phase 2/Phase 3 assessment model with a continuous AI-driven loop that works for ANY target type (website, internal network, external IP, API, domain) and drills as deep as the target allows. The loop: OBSERVE (build current state from all collected evidence) → DECIDE (AI picks next highest-value action) → [APPROVE if needed] → EXECUTE (run chosen action) → OBSERVE (update state with new findings) → repeat until stuck or max depth. Architecture: (1) AssessmentState: at any point the AI sees everything collected so far: { inventory: [hosts, services, endpoints], findings: [vulns found], tested_paths: [what has been run], open_threads: [leads not yet followed], target_type: auto-detected }. (2) AI Decision Engine: given AssessmentState, AI produces NextAction: { tool: <any registered runner>, target: <specific host/endpoint/service>, params: { specific, targeted }, tier: passive|active|intrusive, reasoning: 'Found login form on /admin — next: test default credentials and auth bypass', confidence: 0.85, follow_up_if_successful: 'if credentials work, test admin panel for IDOR and upload vectors' }. (3) Approval gate (tier-based): passive actions auto-proceed; active actions require one wave approval; intrusive actions require per-action explicit approval. Operator sees: 'AI wants to run: auth-flow against /admin (login form found). Reason: test default credentials, auth bypass, session fixation. Tier: active. Approve?' (4) Execution: run the action, capture output, extract new signals into AssessmentState. (5) Loop decision: if new attack surface found → continue loop. If no new findings in last 2 iterations → mark as 'maximum depth reached for current access level'. If intrusive approved → new deeper loop starts. (6) Works universally: for internal network: nmap → finds host → fingerprints service → finds SSH → ssh-brute → if success → priv-esc-linux → finds SUID → [needs intrusive approval] → exploit SUID → root. For website: httpx → finds login form → tests auth bypass → finds upload → tests XSS upload → confirms stored XSS → [active approval] → CSRF chain → admin cookie → admin panel → file write → [intrusive approval] → RCE. The AI follows the attack path, not a script. (7) Depth model: passive (tier 0, auto), active (tier 1, one approval), credential (tier 2, explicit), intrusive (tier 3, per-action), exploitation (tier 4, highest gate). (8) Stuck detection: if 3 consecutive iterations produce no new signals or findings, the loop stops and shows: 'Maximum depth reached at tier N. Next tier requires: [specific approval/credentials/tool].' IMPLEMENTATION: Build on existing ai_agent.py (proposal generation) + backlog-248 (AI shell) + backlog-256 (signals) + backlog-258 (runner metadata). Replace assessment_chain.py fixed phases with this loop for AssessmentMode=AI_DRIVEN. Fixed phases remain available as the manual/deterministic option.
scope: User vision: AI checks target, picks next step, finds things, executes, goes deeper, repeats until stuck at maximum depth. Works for internal network, website, external IP. This is fundamentally different from fixed phases — AI is the orchestrator. AutoPenBench's 64% assisted agent success validates this model. backlog-248 (AI Free Bash) is the execution engine. This task is the loop controller that makes the whole thing work.
generation_reason: User: AI should drive the assessment — observe, decide, execute, repeat until deepest possible state reached. Works for any target type. This is the core intelligence layer.

This task supersedes the planning layer of backlog-255, backlog-257, backlog-259 — those describe data foundations that this task uses, but the loop replaces the fixed-phase execution model.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Loop runs within approved scope only. Each tier escalation requires explicit approval. Stuck detection stops the loop gracefully. Fixed-phase assessment chains remain available as the manual option.
constraints.safety: Tier-based approval gates are non-negotiable: passive auto-proceeds; active requires wave approval; intrusive/exploitation require per-action explicit approval with ROE confirmation. Kill switch stops loop immediately. Maximum 20 loop iterations per engagement to prevent runaway.

success_criteria: Assessment loop starts from any target type (URL, IP, CIDR, domain) without pre-selecting phases.
AI produces NextAction with specific tool, target, params, reasoning, and tier for each iteration.
Active actions show operator approval request: exact tool, target, reasoning visible.
Intrusive actions require explicit per-action approval.
Loop continues automatically after passive/approved actions.
Stuck detection stops loop after 3 iterations with no new signals.
Mission Control shows loop progress: 'Iteration 7: found login form → testing auth bypass → found weak credentials → testing privilege escalation'.
For Gruyere: loop progresses from reflected XSS → file upload XSS → stored XSS → CSRF chain → admin access → path traversal → RCE without operator having to manually select each tool.
For LAN: loop progresses from nmap → service fingerprint → ssh brute → credential → priv-esc → root without fixed phases.
Fixed-phase assessment still works as alternative mode.
No regression in existing assessment chain tests.
must_not_touch: Fixed-phase assessment chains (keep as manual alternative)

acceptance_criteria: Loop starts from URL target and reaches at least 3 iterations without operator picking tools.
Stuck detection works after 3 no-result iterations.
Active tier approval visible in Mission Control.
Gruyere acceptance test passes at least layers 1-4.
LAN target reaches service discovery → credential testing loop.

out_of_scope: Fully autonomous exploitation without approval gates
